name: File Operations
description: Structured file read, write, and edit tools. Prefer edit_file for targeted changes; use write_file only for new files or full rewrites.

tools.name: read_file
tools.description: Read a file with line numbers and total line count. Returns up to 200 lines per call. Always returns total_lines so you know the file size. Use offset+limit to page through large files. Prefer this over shell cat.

path.description: Path to the file to read

offset.description: 0-based line index to start reading from (default: 0)

limit.description: Maximum lines to return, up to 200 (default: 200)

tools.name: write_file
tools.description: Fully overwrite a file or create a new one. If the file already exists, you MUST call read_file first to understand its current content before overwriting. Use for new files, empty file creation (touch), or large rewrites only. For small targeted changes to existing files, use edit_file instead — it is safer and more efficient.

path.description: Path to the file to write

content.description: Full content to write to the file. Omit or pass empty string to create an empty file (touch).

tools.name: edit_file
tools.description: Surgically replace an exact block of text in a file. Read the file first to get the exact content. Provide old_lines (the exact existing text to replace) and new_lines (the replacement). Limited to 100 new lines per call — split larger changes into multiple edit_file calls or use write_file. Fails if old_lines matches 0 or more than 1 location.

path.description: Path to the file to edit

old_lines.description: The exact text to find and replace (must match exactly once in the file)

new_lines.description: The replacement text (max 100 lines; use write_file for larger changes)
